newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares fall on lack of cash, bill auction.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares fall on lack of cash, bill auction.

text.p: Istanbul shares extended morning losses in afternoon selling on Tuesday amid a lack of fresh cash influx and negative auction results, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at 83,723.00, down 969.20 points, or 1.14 percent from Monday's all-time high of 84,692.20. It brushed a high of 85,798 in early trade before sellers stepped in.
Trade volume dived to 16.49 trillion lira from 21.52 trillion on Monday.
"Buying faded because of the lack of fresh cash entry," said Burak Vidinliier from Info securities.
Brokers said afternoon sales accelerated on news of low sale and sharply higher yield in Treasury's 182-day t-bill auction.
It sold 69.62 trillion lira of six-month papers due to thin demand as the maximum yield surged to 135.16 percent from 118.75 in the previous 273-day bill auction on November 5.
Bankers were earlier expecting weak demand and higher yields because of a 10 percent withholding tax imposed on government securities to be issued with 1997 maturity from November 1.
Banks will pay 44.7 trillion lira to the Treasury for the 182-day bills to be issued on Wednesday when 128.1 trillion lira will be cashed in from maturing t-bills.
"Excess cash to be left in the market may be diverted to the dollar tomorrow. The central bank will probably intervene to curb dollar demand," said Yalcin Arican from Hak Securities.

Brokers said the sharp increase in yield would also support upward expectations in t-bill and bond rates. Turkish markets would eye central bank moves to control the U.S. currency's gains and withdraw surplus lira tomorrow, they added.
Brokers said the market failed in its third attempt to pierce the critical 85,000 resistance.

The index had drifted lower in a week-long limited pull back after testing 85,000 on October 31, following a 29.3 percent rally and ten record high closes in a strong medium-term uptrend from September 13 to October 23.

Top actives were utilities Cukurova Elektrik, up 1,000 lira at 85,000, Aktas Elektrik, down 3,000 lira at 100,000 and largely state-owed petroleum refiner Tupras, down 1,000 lira at 21,000. Together, they made up 25 percent of the total volume.

Of the 225 shares traded, falls outdid rises by 134 to 44 and 47 ended unchanged. The 85-share industrial index slipped 0.7 percent lower to 88,617.28 and the 15-share financial index lost 2.11 percent to 80,706.58.
